title: A `/*` or `$$` inside a string or `--` comment breaks the next real comment or dollar-quoted string
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

Text that only looks like a delimiter, because it sits inside a string literal or a `--` comment, is treated as a real one, and the next genuine comment or dollar-quoted literal is then tokenized as garbage.

```python
import sqlparse
sqlparse.format("SELECT '/*' FROM t; /* c */ SELECT 1", strip_comments=True)
```
Expected: `"SELECT '/*' FROM t; SELECT 1"`
Actual: `"SELECT '/*' FROM t;/* c */ SELECT 1"` (the comment is not recognised: `sqlparse.lexer.tokenize` yields `/`, `*`, `c`, ... instead of one `Comment.Multiline` token `'/* c */'`)

Dollar quoting is hit too: in `"-- $$\nDO $$ BEGIN NULL; END $$"` the body should be one `Literal` token `'$$ BEGIN NULL; END $$'`, but the tokens come out as `Error '$'` and keywords.

The rule: `/*`, `*/`, `/*+` and `$$` / `$tag$` that occur inside a single- or double-quoted string or behind `--` are ordinary text and must not affect later comments, optimizer hints or dollar-quoted literals. Also, a closing `$$` may follow the opener immediately, so `SELECT $$$a$$` should give one `Literal` `'$$$a$$'`.

Tokenizing must stay linear on long inputs with many unclosed `/*` or `$$`.
acceptance: Both reported inputs tokenize as expected (one `Comment.Multiline` `'/* c */'`, one `Literal` `'$$ BEGIN NULL; END $$'`)
Look-alike delimiters in strings or `--` comments never affect later `/* */`, `/*+ */`, `$$` or `$tag$` tokens, and `SELECT $$$a$$` gives one literal
Long inputs with many unmatched `/*` or `$$` still tokenize quickly
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
